name: XtremeData dbX
tagline: Parallel, vectorized SQL analytics engine on PostgreSQL roots, once an FPGA appliance, now cloud software.
description: dbX from XtremeData, Inc. of Schaumburg, Illinois, is a massively parallel SQL engine for analytics. The company started from an open-source database package and re-engineered the executor into a parallel, vectorized engine that runs as a single logical database across nodes, so it does not depend on distribution keys or star schemas for performance; it keeps PostgreSQL-compatible SQL and UDFs. Around 2009-2010 dbX shipped as appliances with Altera FPGA accelerators and Cray-based systems; today it is sold as software for AWS, Azure, Google Cloud and on-premises clusters handling up to hundreds of terabytes. The website is maintained, but public release news is scarce.
statusNote: Website still offers dbX for AWS, Azure, GCP and on-prem in 2026, but no public release notes or news have appeared for years.

scale.notes: Vendor positions it for 1 to hundreds of TB, scaling compute and storage independently.

strengths: Complex multi-way joins and aggregates without careful data partitioning
Vectorized, fully parallel executor rather than federated Postgres instances
PostgreSQL-compatible SQL keeps existing tools usable
weaknesses: Small vendor with little public documentation or community
useCases: Cloud or on-prem data warehouses up to hundreds of TB
Complex ad-hoc SQL over large schemas
notIdealFor: Teams wanting an open ecosystem or managed SaaS
